clue.text: Help when one's stuck in position

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'

indicators.note: something stuck in another is lodged within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture
one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: Advice on when to step in: lend a hand to someone stuck in an awkward position.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'one's' expands to 'one is', I plus the verb, rather than marking possession; 'when' is a common crossword stand-in for as.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is a straightforward synonym of help, aid given to someone.

clue.text: Last word from alpha males

parts.note: alpha is the NATO and Greek name for the letter A
males are men

explanation.surface: The alpha males in a group always insist on having the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer, literally the final utterance.

clue.text: Second drink follows drink

indicators.note: one drink coming after the other places the second word at the end

parts.note: to sup is to drink, sipping something
porter is a dark beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A second round of drinks arrives straight after the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is not an ordinal here: a second in a duel or boxing match is a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in a duel or boxing bout is the backer who stands by the fighter, a supporter.

clue.text: Quiet beer possibly source of gas

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A quiet pint of beer might give one wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests beer causing wind; the gas is the natural kind extracted by fracking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale gas is natural gas extracted from shale rock formations.

clue.text: Makes hard queen say less occasionally

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the words say less is taken

explanation.surface: Telling the queen to say less would be making things difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'say less': A, L, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and cools metal or glass to toughen it, a technical sense of hardening.

clue.text: Struggle with advance embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to come is to advance or approach
pet is a term of endearment, a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to make an advance while embracing their sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to strive or contend against rivals, a struggle for a prize.

clue.text: Drive with parking on slope

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force something in
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Instructions for driving into a car park built on an incline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface joining two levels, a slope.

clue.text: Conscious of strife in hospital department

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is the UK hospital casualty department
war is strife or conflict

explanation.surface: A staff member is conscious of the conflict raging in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (accident and emergency) is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware of something is knowing about or noticing it, conscious of it.

clue.text: Joke from proletariat about Labour's leader

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the class word goes round the letter

parts.note: the peasantry is the class of poor labourers, a proletariat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here that of Labour's

explanation.surface: A political quip from the working class about the head of the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; the first letter of Labour's is L, set inside PEASANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light jocular remark, a little quip or joke.

clue.text: Endless dessert, also called foreign delicacy

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert
aka is the abbreviation for also known as, meaning also called

explanation.surface: An unfinished pudding that also goes by the name of an exotic treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced lamb, a foreign speciality.

clue.text: Defend former partner left in drag

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in places one letter within the other word

parts.note: a drag is a tiresome nuisance, a pain

explanation.surface: Someone justifying their ex who was found in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' is not cross-dressing here but a bore or nuisance, a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain one's conduct is to justify it, offering a defence.

clue.text: Say, a space turned into berth

indicators.note: turned means put round the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
room is space

explanation.surface: A space made over into a sleeping berth on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: EG, A and ROOM, read backwards together, give the answer; 'into' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place for a vessel, or the charge for one, is where a ship berths.

clue.text: Analysis of chap facing madness

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
rage is fury, a kind of madness

explanation.surface: A psychiatric study of a man confronting insanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' is a link word putting one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: News coverage is the reporting and analysis given to a story.

clue.text: Pips best players

definitions.meaning: pips are the small ... of fruit
in a tournament the top players are seeded

explanation.surface: Pips the best players to the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Pips are fruit seeds, and top-ranked tournament entrants are seeds.

clue.text: Wretched 'celebs' paid to go wild

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Paying celebrities to behave outrageously is a contemptible business.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable means deserving contempt, a sense of wretched as vile.

clue.text: Buries old doctors on hospital department

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: ENT, ear, nose and throat, is a hospital department
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree, so MBs are doctors

explanation.surface: Former physicians bury their mistakes on the ear, nose and throat ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to put a body in a tomb, to bury it.

clue.text: Beneath sea one finds tarry anchor

indicators.note: in a down clue the word below comes second

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
to tarry is to stay or linger

explanation.surface: Under the sea a diver comes upon an anchor coated with tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarry' looks like 'covered in tar' but is the verb to linger; 'one finds' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief support, figuratively an anchor for a family or team.

clue.text: Excuse could be so naive

indicators.note: could be signals the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A remark that a feeble excuse might seem naive.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasion is a dodge or pretext for avoiding something, an excuse.

clue.text: Halfwit on air with smug broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A dim presenter who is complacent while on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Blocks forces capturing a rook

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the word holds the pieces inside

parts.note: to prise or pry open is to force, so pries means forces
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess game where blocking pieces force the capture of a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry a blow is to ward it off, blocking it.

clue.text: Possibly dirty small talk

parts.note: patter is glib talk

explanation.surface: Small talk that might be smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' makes the definition fair: spattering may soil something, though not always.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to splash with drops, which can soil a surface.

clue.text: Student more inadequate taking arithmetic?

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: leaner means thinner, scantier, so more inadequate
arithmetic is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: A weaker student taking a maths class.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so arithmetic can stand for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is one who is studying, a student or pupil.

clue.text: Share applications for plants

parts.note: a lot is one's share or portion
uses are applications

explanation.surface: A shared software release for running industrial plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotuses are water lilies, a group of aquatic plants.

clue.text: Complete havoc, anarchy or shambles initially

definitions.text: Complete havoc, anarchy or shambles initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A description of total disorder: havoc, anarchy, a shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and its first letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder and confusion, which the listed words all describe.

clue.text: A sailor turns up world map

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives with a map of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps of the world.

clue.text: Sweetheart is trying to retain style

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the answer is kept inside these words

explanation.surface: A lover making an effort to keep up their style.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or flair, the style shown in a work.

clue.text: Actress's last desire to be fashionable

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Actress's

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: An actress's final wish is to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart or stylish, so fashionable.

clue.text: Reportedly makes vases

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: to make money is to earn it, so makes means earns

explanation.surface: A rumour about who makes vases.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent earns and urns sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are large vases, often for ashes.

clue.text: Capital is strong following detailed warning

indicators.note: the strong word follows the trimmed warning
detailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a bell sounds a warning
fast means firm and strong, as in holding fast

explanation.surface: A city's resilience after a detailed warning was issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, BELL losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Cook, large inside, getting more slender

indicators.note: inside places the letter within the cooking word

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A chef who used to be large is now getting thinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmer is the comparative of slim, meaning thinner or more slender.

clue.text: Language is Queen's English

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: The King's English was once the Queen's English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Dodgy hip, so rests hip replacement?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: With a bad hip, one rests until it is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: a replacement hip is one kind of prosthesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, of which an artificial hip joint is an instance.
